title: Revisiting Deep Learning Models for Tabular Data
claim: ResNet-like tabular models are useful competitive baselines; this is not evidence of HDD superiority.
hypothesis: Residual blocks on compressed SMART window summaries can learn nonlinear interactions.

title: An Empirical Evaluation of Generic Convolutional and Recurrent Networks for Sequence Modeling
claim: Convolutional sequence models warrant comparison with recurrent models across sequence tasks.
hypothesis: A small dilated temporal convolution plus SMART summaries captures short-term degradation. The implementation is an adaptation, not a paper reproduction.

claim: SMART attribute availability varies by vendor, and daily history can have gaps.
hypothesis: Observation masks and vendor indicators distinguish missing counters from observed zero counters.

claim: Historical ML supplies critical-counter growth features. A three-seed paired ablation on reused HDD validation improved ROS and F1 in all three seeds, but mean precision and AUPRC fell and false alarms rose. This supports an optional feature branch, not universal superiority.

empirical_evidence.limitations: Only one architecture/configuration tested; no full-paper causal or held-out generalization claim.

hypothesis: Critical-counter growth and nonzero frequency can help a neural model distinguish degradation from vendor-specific absolute levels.

claim: Threshold-ratio fold alignment at threshold_scale=1 improved mean ROS by only 0.0822 against raw scores at the same scale, while AUPRC fell in all seeds. Against original raw scale1.2, aligned scale1 reduced mean ROS by 0.6213 and increased FAR. Keep raw calibration as default; do not attribute scale changes to alignment.
hypothesis: Retain only as an optional experimental branch, not a demonstrated default improvement.

claim: For frozen hybrid candidate 31, jointly using replicas=1, lr=0.001 and epochs=30 improved ROS and F1 in all three matched seeds and reduced mean runtime from 25.40 to 10.63 seconds. Mean precision fell and FAR rose. This tests a joint alternative, not a causal effect of any one parameter.
hypothesis: Prefer testing this cheaper starting point while retaining predictive and runtime comparisons.

claim: At 25% tree blending, ROS, AUPRC and low-FAR recall improved in all three matched seeds; mean deltas +1.0650, +0.01805, +0.00750. Mean precision fell by 0.00457, FAR rose by 0.0000553, runtime rose by 1.27 seconds. This is ML+DL, not pure DL or a reproduction of historical ML.
hypothesis: Check whether tree partitions and neural temporal features make complementary errors; report added training cost.

claim: A three-seed fixed-config ablation on reused validation improved ROS, F1 and F1_p10 in all seeds. Mean ROS +1.1251, precision +0.00826, recall +0.01191, AUPRC +0.00398, FAR -0.000111. Low-FAR recall improved in only one seed despite positive mean; runtime increased in all seeds. Promising initial features, not universal superiority.
hypothesis: Expose device scale and observation gaps explicitly while distinguishing counter resets from degradation.

claim: Weighted hard-negative ranking increased recall but reduced precision and increased false alarms in all three matched seeds. Mean ROS changed by -1.4172 at weight 0.1 and -0.3471 at 0.3. Weight 0.3 improved mean AUPRC by 0.00659, so further calibration is an unverified possibility, not a demonstrated overall gain.
hypothesis: Only retain ranking as an optional branch; investigate precision/recall tradeoffs without claiming it solves low-FAR recall.

claim: Frozen search candidate 25 exceeded all predictive metrics of three ML baselines at search seed 20261020, but failed that gate on new seeds 20261201..20261203. Mean ROS 40.6940, recall 0.41799, F1 0.41628 and low-FAR recall 0.47795 fell below the strong ML baseline; precision 0.41540 and FAR 0.001478 remained favorable. Candidate 0 also failed the all-seed gate, with mean ROS 40.9457 and low-FAR recall 0.47972. Lowering the final threshold alone cannot repair ranking at a fixed FAR.
hypothesis: Treat single-seed comprehensive wins as provisional. Test ranking improvements and train-only calibration separately, then freeze configurations before new training-seed checks; do not select seeds using validation outcomes.

claim: Changing only frozen candidate 25 epoch selection from AUPRC to operational_proxy reduced ROS, recall and F1 in all three matched seeds. Mean deltas were ROS -0.62746, F1 -0.00912 and low-FAR recall -0.00794. Mean precision improved 0.01422 and FAR fell 0.000345, but this did not solve the comprehensive-metric objective.
hypothesis: Keep AUPRC as the default epoch criterion; investigate representation quality rather than assuming the composite early-stop proxy improves deployment metrics.

claim: Replacing TCN with dual TCN+GRU at otherwise identical candidate-25 settings improved precision, low-FAR recall and FAR in all three matched seeds: mean deltas +0.01474, +0.00397, -0.000278. Recall fell in every seed (mean -0.03351), and mean ROS fell 0.08428. GRU alone improved AUPRC in all seeds but not comprehensive performance. No architecture passed all-seed superiority.
hypothesis: Test train-only threshold calibration for dual as a separate paired intervention; the observed ranking gains do not establish comprehensive superiority.

claim: Reducing dual threshold_scale from 1.2 to 1.0 raised recall in all three matched seeds (mean +0.07055), but lowered precision in all seeds (-0.05715) and raised FAR (+0.0008). Mean ROS fell 0.41902 and F1 fell 0.00948. AUPRC and low-FAR recall were exactly unchanged, consistent with unchanged scores.
hypothesis: Retain the original threshold for this configuration. Further gains require better ranking or representation, not merely relaxing alarms.

claim: For frozen candidate 10, stratified training-OOF bootstrap median thresholds produced mean ROS -0.04751, precision -0.01625, recall +0.01587 and FAR +0.000155 versus empirical thresholds. ROS improved in no seed. AUPRC and low-FAR recall were unchanged. This did not establish better comprehensive performance or reduced between-seed instability.
hypothesis: Retain empirical thresholds. Test informative representations instead of assuming threshold smoothing improves model quality.

claim: Adding model-identity one-hot features to candidate 10 increased recall in all three matched seeds, but mean ROS fell 0.37068, AUPRC fell 0.00159 and low-FAR recall fell 0.00882. FAR did not improve in any seed. Explicit model identity did not establish a comprehensive benefit for this configuration.
hypothesis: Keep model identity optional and disabled by default; investigate measurement features without assuming categorical metadata helps.

claim: Restricting candidate 10 to fixed SMART IDs 5/9/187/188/194/197/198/199 reduced ROS, precision, F1, AUPRC and low-FAR recall in all three matched seeds. Mean deltas: ROS -2.66493, F1 -0.02627, AUPRC -0.03001, low-FAR recall -0.02028. Runtime fell 4.74 seconds on average, but predictive performance deteriorated. This tests a fixed subset, not all possible feature selection methods.
hypothesis: Keep all SMART measurements for this configuration; do not treat domain familiarity as proof that omitted attributes are irrelevant.

claim: Changing candidate 10 positive_boost from 3 to 1 in both neural and tree branches reduced mean ROS 0.46950, F1 0.01142 and recall 0.03704. AUPRC fell in all three seeds (mean -0.00487). Mean precision improved 0.02110, FAR fell 0.0002 and low-FAR recall rose 0.00705, so the intervention changes tradeoffs but does not establish comprehensive superiority. Original entity weights were preserved.
hypothesis: Retain the existing joint weighting for this configuration; any branch-specific weighting experiment must be evaluated separately.

claim: At candidate-10 settings, changing only tree positive boost from 3 to 1 yielded mean ROS -0.02324, F1 +0.00356, AUPRC -0.00644, recall -0.02116; ROS improved in two seeds. Changing only neural positive boost from 3 to 1 yielded mean ROS +0.01427 but improved ROS in only one seed and reduced AUPRC in all three (mean -0.00272). Neither intervention establishes comprehensive benefit or stable improvement.
hypothesis: Retain joint boost 3 by default. Independent branch weighting remains an optional hypothesis, not an empirically established improvement.

claim: Appending daily log-value differences with adjacent-day observation masks to candidate 10 produced mean ROS -0.03306, F1 +0.00215, AUPRC +0.00029 and precision -0.02355. Low-FAR recall improved in no seed (mean -0.00662), and runtime increased in all seeds (+1.14 seconds). One higher ROS seed does not establish a stable comprehensive gain.
hypothesis: Keep the new delta channels disabled by default; retain existing tabular trend features and evaluate other temporal representations separately.

claim: Adding temporal maximum activation pooling to candidate 10 reduced mean ROS 0.23140, precision 0.01110, F1 0.00129 and AUPRC 0.00082. Low-FAR recall improved in no seed (mean -0.00265), and runtime increased in all seeds (mean +1.02 seconds). Mean recall rose 0.01544 but FAR rose 0.000167. Keeping peaks did not establish a comprehensive gain.
hypothesis: Retain mean-and-last temporal aggregation by default; more aggregation features are not automatically better.

claim: Transferring window range and last-minus-mean features from the inspected strong ML program to candidate 10 yielded mean ROS -0.57468, F1 -0.00830, recall -0.02028 and AUPRC -0.00420. AUPRC fell in all three matched seeds. Mean precision and low-FAR recall improved slightly, but runtime rose in every seed (+1.87 seconds). Useful features in the source ML model did not establish benefit in this hybrid configuration.
hypothesis: Keep window contrasts disabled by default; transferred priors must remain testable hypotheses, not automatic promotions.

claim: At candidate-10 settings, width 256 versus 128 improved ROS, precision, F1 and AUPRC in all three matched seeds (mean +0.31942, +0.03021, +0.00487, +0.00296). FAR fell in all seeds (-0.000367), as did runtime (-1.80 seconds), but recall fell in all seeds (-0.03219). Width 64 reduced mean ROS and F1. The larger network is a promising branch, not comprehensive superiority.
hypothesis: Evaluate a modest train-only threshold adjustment for the larger network while preserving all baseline and seed checks.

claim: At width 256, reducing threshold_scale from 1.2 to 1.1 raised recall in every matched seed (mean +0.03395) but lowered precision in every seed (-0.02408) and raised FAR (+0.000356). Mean ROS fell 0.01960 and F1 fell 0.00220. AUPRC and low-FAR recall remained identical. The modest adjustment did not deliver comprehensive improvement.
hypothesis: Preserve the existing threshold; focus subsequent work on ranking quality rather than trading precision for recall.

claim: Parameter EMA decay 0.99 versus disabled at candidate-10 settings reduced mean ROS by 0.06790 and F1 by 0.00123. AUPRC fell in every matched seed (mean -0.00132); runtime increased in every seed (+3.16 seconds). Mean precision increased 0.01211 and low-FAR recall increased 0.00221, but recall fell 0.00882. Only one seed improved ROS. This does not establish stable or comprehensive benefit.
hypothesis: Keep EMA disabled by default. Prioritize stronger predictive representations or branch training over repeating this unsupported averaging intervention.

claim: Increasing the hybrid tree branch from 150 to 300 rounds at candidate-10 settings gave mean ROS +0.09443, F1 +0.00415 and AUPRC +0.00118, but ROS improved in only one matched seed. Mean precision fell 0.00653, low-FAR recall fell 0.00573, FAR rose 0.000078 and runtime increased in all seeds (+2.88 seconds). This does not establish comprehensive superiority.
hypothesis: Keep 150 rounds as default. More rounds alone are not a reliable improvement; evaluate complementary tree structure or representation separately.

claim: Increasing tree leaves from 15 to 31 at fixed 150 rounds reduced ROS and recall in all three matched seeds (mean -0.83133 and -0.03659). Mean F1 fell 0.01400, AUPRC fell 0.00189 and low-FAR recall fell 0.00088. Precision improved in all seeds (+0.00725) and FAR fell in all seeds (-0.000178), but runtime increased in all seeds (+1.48 seconds). This is a tradeoff, not comprehensive improvement.
hypothesis: Retain 15 leaves by default; larger tree capacity has not established a benefit at the current hybrid settings.

claim: At fixed candidate-10 models and weights, logit versus probability fusion reduced ROS, precision and F1 in every matched seed (mean -0.34555, -0.01070, -0.00499). Recall increased in every seed (+0.00573), but FAR also increased in every seed (+0.000122). Mean AUPRC fell 0.00285 and low-FAR recall fell 0.00088. Changing the fusion rule did not establish ranking or comprehensive benefit.
hypothesis: Retain probability fusion by default. Do not interpret increased recall at worse false alarms as comprehensive improvement.

claim: Feeding the tree pre-normalization engineered features instead of the neural normalized features reduced ROS, recall, F1 and F1-p10 in every matched seed (mean -0.42875, -0.00926, -0.00632, -0.00679). Mean AUPRC fell 0.00032 and low-FAR recall fell 0.00397. Runtime improved in all seeds (-0.75 seconds), but this did not compensate for predictive degradation.
hypothesis: Retain normalized tree input by default. The suspected preprocessing bottleneck was not supported by this controlled experiment.

claim: Selecting neural checkpoints by blended inner AP instead of standalone neural AP reduced recall, F1 and AUPRC in all three matched seeds (mean -0.03131, -0.00838, -0.00502). Mean ROS fell 0.36695, improving in only one seed. FAR fell in every seed (-0.000189), and mean precision rose 0.00995, but the result is a tradeoff rather than comprehensive gain.
hypothesis: Keep standalone neural checkpoint selection by default. Improving the blended inner objective did not translate into improved external ranking in this experiment.

claim: Replacing train-only maximum absolute temporal channel scaling with the 99th percentile reduced ROS, F1, F1-p10 and AUPRC in all three matched seeds (mean -0.70695, -0.01180, -0.01015, -0.00605). Mean recall rose 0.02116, but precision fell 0.03643 and FAR rose 0.000345. Runtime increased in every seed (+1.20 seconds). Robust scaling did not establish ranking or comprehensive benefit here.
hypothesis: Retain max-absolute sequence scaling by default. The suspected outlier compression bottleneck was not supported by this intervention.

claim: A 48-candidate search with updated evidence did not improve the incumbent configurations. Both selected incumbents failed all-seed comprehensive predictive and resource gates on seeds 20270210-20270212. Candidate 0 mean F1/AUPRC/recall/low-FAR recall were 0.42371/0.39120/0.42372/0.47619; candidate 1 means were 0.40565/0.39048/0.44224/0.47266. Single-search-seed gains remain unstable; new training seeds are not independent generalization evidence.
hypothesis: The current search has plateaued. Investigate a materially different training or representation mechanism rather than repeat the same local search and claim progress from selected seeds.

claim: Training neural log-odds corrections to a fixed tree versus separate probability averaging reduced AUPRC in all three matched seeds (mean -0.01029). Mean ROS fell 0.32697, precision fell 0.01641 and low-FAR recall fell 0.00397. F1 rose 0.00451 and recall rose 0.00882 on average, but ROS improved in only one seed. In-sample tree priors did not establish comprehensive benefit.
hypothesis: Keep residual training disabled. A further residual experiment should address in-sample tree-prior optimism rather than assume that additive correction improves ranking.

claim: Cross-fitted versus in-sample tree priors for residual learning reduced F1 and F1-p10 in all three matched seeds (mean -0.01132 and -0.01029). Mean ROS fell 0.61162 and AUPRC fell 0.00323; ROS improved in only one seed. Runtime increased in every seed (+2.93 seconds). Bootstrap F1 variability fell in every seed, but predictive performance did not comprehensively improve. This comparison also changes tree training size and query ensembling.
hypothesis: Keep cross-fitted residual learning disabled; neither tested residual approach establishes a replacement for separate model averaging.

title: TabM: Advancing Tabular Deep Learning with Parameter-Efficient Ensembling
claim: TabM shares most parameters among implicit MLP ensemble members. Official guidance requires averaging individual member losses during training and averaging class probabilities at inference. Published tabular benchmark results do not establish HDD superiority. Official tabm 0.0.3 passed a small GPU forward/backward compatibility check in this environment.
hypothesis: Test an optional official TabM backend on the existing engineered HDD inputs with fixed folds, train-only calibration and explicit runtime accounting. Do not substitute the loss of averaged predictions for memberwise training.

claim: The first TCN plus official TabM-8 backend comparison retained three outer replicas and used two TabM blocks versus the original residual block. Recall rose in all seeds (+0.02690), but precision fell in all seeds (-0.02494), FAR rose in all seeds (+0.000311), and runtime increased in all seeds (+12.56 seconds). Mean ROS/F1/AUPRC changed -0.14799/-0.00409/-0.00242. No comprehensive benefit was established; this is not a pure member-count ablation or a tuned TabM benchmark.
hypothesis: Keep the original backend as default. Evaluate an explicitly budgeted TabM-specific training configuration before drawing broad conclusions about the architecture.

claim: For the fixed TCN+TabM-8 configuration, official optimizer starting values lr=0.002 and weight_decay=0.0003 versus inherited 0.0003/0.001 reduced ROS and F1-p10 in every matched seed (mean -0.19997 and -0.00537). Mean F1/AUPRC changed -0.00448/-0.00242; low-FAR recall rose 0.00705 on average. Runtime fell in every seed (-9.86 seconds). This is a speed versus predictive tradeoff, not comprehensive improvement or evidence against all TabM tuning.
hypothesis: Retain inherited optimizer values for the current comparison; treat the official starting point as an optional efficiency branch, not a universally better setting.

claim: For fixed TCN+TabM-8, periodic numerical embeddings improved ROS and low-FAR recall in all three seeds (mean +0.41796 and +0.01146). Mean precision/F1/AUPRC changed +0.02189/+0.00447/+0.00097, but recall fell in two seeds and tied once (mean -0.01852). FAR improved twice and tied once. Bootstrap F1 spread and runtime worsened in every seed (+0.00121 and +23.77 seconds). This is not comprehensive improvement; embeddings also affect official backend initialization.
hypothesis: Keep embeddings experimental. Since TabM already ensembles internal members, test reducing outer replicas with a fixed paired budget to investigate overhead, while explicitly checking recall and all baseline gates. Do not infer independent generalization from reused validation seeds.

claim: For periodic-embedding TCN+TabM-8 at fixed total training budget, reducing outer replicas from three to one improved AUPRC in every seed (+0.00292 mean) and reduced runtime in every seed (-38.57 seconds). Mean ROS changed +0.07713 but won only once; precision/F1/low-FAR recall changed -0.01070/-0.00066/-0.00176, while recall rose +0.02469 and FAR rose +0.000244. Low-FAR recall never strictly improved. This is an efficiency tradeoff, not comprehensive superiority. Per-model time allowance increases when replicas decrease.
hypothesis: Keep the single-replica TabM branch as an explicit efficiency candidate; compare a fixed standalone TabM input against the TCN hybrid before adding complexity. Retain all predictive and resource gates.

claim: Removing the TCN branch from single-replica periodic TabM-8 with unchanged tree fusion reduced runtime in all seeds (-3.08 seconds mean). ROS won twice but averaged -0.05401; mean F1/AUPRC changed -0.00173/-0.00220. Recall and low-FAR recall rose +0.01499/+0.00529 on average, while precision fell -0.01633 and FAR rose +0.000155. This does not establish comprehensive superiority for either branch and includes changed input dimensions and initialization.
hypothesis: Retain both explicit candidates without promoting either on ROS alone. Evaluate whether internal ensemble size improves the single-replica TCN TabM branch under the same total budget before extending automatic search.

claim: For single-replica periodic TCN+TabM at fixed total training budget, increasing internal members from 8 to 16 reduced ROS/F1/F1-p10 in every seed (mean -0.33141/-0.00644/-0.00629) and increased runtime in every seed (+9.65 seconds). Mean AUPRC changed +0.00061, low-FAR recall -0.00176, precision -0.00975 and recall -0.00309. Larger internal ensemble did not establish comprehensive benefit.
hypothesis: Keep eight members as the current experimental starting point. Before further model-size changes, compare a bounded learning-rate adjustment for the single-replica periodic backend; do not transfer the earlier three-replica optimizer result as proof for this configuration.

claim: For single-replica periodic TCN+TabM-8, changing only lr from 0.0003 to 0.001 improved precision and FAR in all three seeds (+0.02187 and -0.000267 mean) and reduced runtime in all seeds (-4.71 seconds), but recall declined in every seed (-0.02822) and F1 bootstrap spread increased in every seed (+0.00085). Mean ROS/AUPRC changed +0.06894/+0.00410, while F1/F1-p10 changed -0.00025/-0.00108. Low-FAR recall mean was unchanged. No comprehensive benefit was established.
hypothesis: Retain the original learning rate as the reference. The faster setting is a precision/recall tradeoff, not a default upgrade. Consolidate TabM evidence before further isolated parameter changes, and require paired baseline gates for any promoted candidate.

claim: The first integrated TabM search completed 48 valid unique configurations. Only three used TabM (trials 4, 5, 27), with best TabM ROS 41.88529. Original-network references remained ROS-best 42.53068 and weakest-predictive-gap best 42.50064. Six knowledge proposals were recorded, four executed unchanged; trials 31 and 47 were altered and cannot be attributed to their proposed changes. No candidate passed all predictive plus resource gates. This is limited backend exploration, not evidence that all TabM configurations are inferior.
hypothesis: Allocate explicit exploration slots by backend and select parents within each backend, while preserving global comparison and fixed budgets. Test this search-policy change in a new frozen campaign; do not modify the running verification.

claim: Automatic verification after the 48-trial integrated search evaluated the two selected original-network references six times successfully. Neither passed all-seed predictive or resource-inclusive gates. Candidate 0 mean ROS/F1/AUPRC/recall were 41.23268/0.42412/0.39178/0.45459; candidate 1 means were 40.85144/0.41372/0.39119/0.42725. A favorable search seed is not stable comprehensive superiority. This verification did not select a TabM candidate and is not independent generalization evidence.
hypothesis: Continue searching with explicit backend exploration rather than promoting the reference on its search score. Preserve baseline gates and report recall, FAR, stability and runtime failures.

claim: Backend quotas yielded 48 valid unique trials: 18 original, 15 TabM-none, 15 TabM-periodic. Best TabM ROS was 42.29671, below the original reference 42.53068. Five of six knowledge proposals executed unchanged. Both globally selected original-network candidates failed all-seed predictive and resource-inclusive gates in six valid verification evaluations. Candidate 0 mean ROS/F1/AUPRC were 41.19482/0.42464/0.39122; candidate 1 means were 40.84941/0.41940/0.38858. More backend coverage did not establish overall predictive improvement or independent generalization.
hypothesis: Avoid treating more search trials as a substitute for a better objective. Examine the missing low-FAR recall and runtime tradeoffs, then test explicit resource-aware candidate selection while retaining predictive gates; do not promote candidates based on aggregate ROS alone.

claim: After 48 valid unique trials, nine verification evaluations were valid but none of the three selected candidates passed all-seed predictive or resource-inclusive gates. The resource-ranked candidate 45 averaged ROS32.96162/F1 0.35651/AUPRC0.28370/low-FAR recall0.39065 at 4.33 seconds. Original references averaged ROS41.79930 and 41.66919 at 23.55 and 27.12 seconds. Including uncapped relative runtime gaps in worst-gap ranking favored fast but predictively weak candidates; it did not establish comprehensive benefit.
hypothesis: Retain predictive acceptance gates. Inspect objective scaling and prefer predictive-feasible efficiency selection over raw runtime-dominated worst-gap ranking; verify any new policy on a frozen bounded campaign without claiming independent generalization.

claim: Predictive-feasible resource replay selected candidate 3, but six valid paired evaluations of frozen candidates 1 and 3 failed all-seed predictive and resource-inclusive gates. Candidate 3 changed batch size 512 to 1024 and epochs 60 to 30 jointly. Mean runtime improved by 6.48667 seconds in all three pairs, while low-FAR recall fell by 0.00750 in all three. Mean ROS/F1/AUPRC changed by -0.21462/-0.00088/-0.0007167. This is a joint configuration comparison, not isolated epoch causality or independent generalization.
hypothesis: Do not promote the replay winner on single-seed feasibility or runtime alone. Retain low-FAR recall gates and prioritize stable ranking improvement over additional efficiency reductions.

claim: Changing only ranking_weight from 0 to 0.01 on the current three-fold, three-replica hybrid reference produced six valid evaluations. AUPRC improved in all three pairs (mean +0.0020267), but low-FAR recall changed -0.0039633 with only one win. Mean ROS/F1/F1-p10 changed -0.11582/-0.0012967/-0.0019467; FAR increased 0.0001003 and runtime increased 3.32 seconds with no runtime wins. Both configurations failed all-seed predictive and resource gates. Improved global ranking did not imply improved low-FAR ordering; this is not independent generalization evidence.
hypothesis: Keep weak ranking optional, not default. Investigate why batch top-16 negative ranking helps global AP but not the stricter operational tail before changing ranking strength again.

claim: At fixed ranking weight 0.01, reducing batch hard-negative count from 16 to 1 improved low-FAR recall in all three pairs (mean +0.00838) and reduced measured runtime in all three (-2.17667 seconds), but AUPRC fell in all three (-0.00751). Mean ROS/F1/F1-p10 improved +0.31817/+0.0066367/+0.0075167 with only two wins each; recall changed -0.0004433. All six evaluations were valid; neither configuration passed all-seed predictive or resource gates. This compares two ranking configurations, not ranking against zero, and is not independent generalization evidence.
hypothesis: Retain top-1 as an experimental tail-ranking branch, not a default. Its consistent low-FAR benefit versus top-16 trades against global AP; any follow-up must include the no-ranking reference and retain all acceptance gates.

claim: Direct top-1 ranking at weight 0.01 versus no ranking yielded six valid evaluations. AUPRC decreased in every pair (mean -0.0037167), and runtime increased in every pair (+2.51667 seconds). Mean low-FAR recall changed -0.0000033 with only one strict win. ROS improved in two seeds but averaged -0.187609; mean F1/recall changed -0.0027233/-0.0079367. Neither configuration passed all-seed predictive or resource gates. Earlier gains against top-16 did not demonstrate gains against no ranking; these are reused-validation training-seed comparisons, not independent generalization.
hypothesis: Do not promote batch top-1 ranking or keep tuning its strength without a new mechanism. Preserve the no-ranking reference and seek improvements outside this unsuccessful ranking branch.

claim: Appending validity indicators to summary features produced six valid paired evaluations. Mean ROS/AUPRC/recall changed +0.030488/+0.0021767/+0.0211667, but ROS won only one seed. Mean precision/F1/low-FAR recall changed -0.0136933/-0.00182/-0.00353, FAR increased +0.0002223, and runtime increased in all three pairs (+8.27667 seconds). Both configurations failed all-seed predictive and resource gates. This changes the representation of both neural and tree branches, not just missing-value semantics; no independent generalization was established.
hypothesis: Keep tab_missing_indicators disabled by default. Additional indicators substantially increased cost without stable predictive benefit; investigate selective or compact representations rather than promoting all appended masks.

claim: Replacing three TCN replicas with one TCN, GRU and MLP under the same total training budget produced six valid evaluations. ROS/F1/F1-p10 declined in all three pairs, averaging -0.632438/-0.0103667/-0.0103767. Low-FAR recall had zero strict wins and mean -0.00353; AUPRC changed -0.0014367. Runtime improved in all three pairs by a mean 0.71667 seconds. Both configurations failed all-seed predictive and resource gates. This architecture mixture did not establish a diversity benefit or independent generalization.
hypothesis: Retain homogeneous TCN replicas as the reference. Do not assume adding structurally different but individually weaker members improves the ensemble; require direct evidence for any alternative mixture.

claim: Fitting quantiles on the full inner-training fold versus a 10000-row subsample produced six valid evaluations. Recall and AUPRC improved in all three pairs (mean +0.0414467/+0.00229), and bootstrap F1 std declined in all three (-0.0005733). Precision declined in every pair (-0.0405733), FAR increased in every pair (+0.0004667), and F1-p10 had zero strict wins (-0.0056867). Mean ROS/F1/low-FAR recall changed -0.2065825/-0.00555/+0.00044. Neither configuration passed all-seed predictive or resource gates; this is not independent generalization.
hypothesis: Keep the default quantile subsample unchanged. Full-fold fitting showed consistent AP gains but an unfavorable alarm operating point; any calibration follow-up must be fitted only on inner training/OOF data and evaluated directly against the unchanged reference.

claim: Nine evaluations of the original reference, full-fold quantiles and full-fold quantiles with an OOF FAR floor were valid. The 0.002 OOF budget produced identical reported predictive metrics to the uncalibrated full-fold configuration in every seed; only measured runtimes differed. Against the original reference, calibrated full-fold mean ROS/AUPRC/low-FAR recall changed +0.0032741/+0.0009033/+0.0039633, but recall/F1/F1-p10 changed -0.0211633/-0.0015567/-0.0020667. No configuration passed all-seed predictive or resource gates. These results do not prove the threshold was numerically unchanged, only that reported predictive metrics were unchanged; no independent generalization evidence exists.
hypothesis: Do not promote the FAR floor or infer improved external control from its training budget. Instrument train-only threshold diagnostics before any stricter calibration experiment, instead of tuning budgets against external validation.

claim: Train-only replay for seeds 20270411/12/13 found the 0.002 FAR floor inactive in every run: scaled base thresholds were 0.716197/0.584512/0.802108, versus floors 0.486579/0.534992/0.552479. OOF FAR was 0.0007003/0.0016339/0.0005335 and changed OOF alarm counts were all zero. This explains the lack of additional effect in the calibration comparison. These diagnostics are not new benchmark scores or independent generalization evidence.
hypothesis: Do not tighten an already inactive FAR floor merely to force an effect. The reference thresholds are conservative on OOF data; inspect calibration transfer and score aggregation before proposing another alarm restriction.

claim: Shared 10-percent training calibration with matched nine-model averaging produced six valid evaluations. Relative to ordinary OOF, mean ROS/recall/F1/F1-p10/AUPRC/low-FAR recall changed -0.893765/-0.0458567/-0.0164/-0.01415/-0.00474/-0.0022033. Mean precision improved 0.0115533 and FAR decreased 0.000222, but neither configuration passed all-seed predictive or resource gates. Only one seed improved ROS. This recipe also reduced each model's training fraction and calibration sample count, so the regression cannot be attributed solely to matching ensemble aggregation; it is not independent generalization evidence.
hypothesis: Retain ordinary OOF as the reference. Matching aggregation by reducing available training and calibration data did not yield a stable benefit; avoid treating structural consistency alone as empirical improvement.

claim: Three-layer causal dilations 1/2/4 versus the local two-layer TCN produced six valid evaluations. F1 declined in all three pairs (mean -0.0106167); mean ROS/recall/F1-p10/AUPRC changed -0.4827434/-0.01764/-0.00977/-0.00186. Mean low-FAR recall improved +0.0030867 with two wins, insufficient for either configuration to pass all-seed predictive or resource gates. Longer receptive field also changed depth and parameter count, so this is a whole-architecture comparison, not isolated receptive-field causality or independent generalization.
hypothesis: Keep local temporal context as the reference. Full-window causal coverage alone did not provide comprehensive gains; do not expand this branch based on receptive-field arguments without a new empirical mechanism.

claim: Across 30 treatment evaluations from ten selected completed paired campaigns, AUPRC strictly exceeded the strong 4016914b ML baseline every time. Low-FAR recall failed strict superiority 26 times (one tie), F1-p10 25 times, F1 23 times, and runtime 30 times. These selected experiments share validation data; counts are descriptive, not independent trials or generalization probabilities. No treatment passed its all-seed predictive gate.
hypothesis: Prioritize the low-FAR ranking and cost bottlenecks, rather than pursuing global AP gains alone. Preserve the reference while investigating tail-specific errors and training-only alternatives; prior operational-proxy and ranking failures still apply.

title: When AUC meets DRO: Optimizing Partial AUC for Deep Learning with Non-Convex Convergence Guarantee
claim: CVaR partial-AUC optimization uses persistent positive-example auxiliary variables to focus on a bounded false-positive region. It is different from independently selecting batch top-k negatives. Transfer to this weighted HDD benchmark is untested.
hypothesis: Prototype an explicitly weighted persistent-state objective as a separate experimental loss, first checking gradients, state isolation and tiny-tail behavior. Do not label the adaptation as an exact official implementation or assume its convergence guarantee transfers. Keep old batch ranking disabled.

title: Closing the Approximation Gap of Partial AUC Optimization: A Tale of Two Formulations
claim: This 2025 paper studies approximation and scalability limits in partial-AUC optimization and proposes instance-wise minimax reformulations. Its abstract highlights dependence on the constrained region and sample counts; no HDD performance has been established here.
hypothesis: Treat extremely narrow FPR regions as an estimation problem as well as an optimization problem. Audit effective negative support and weight handling before interpreting gains from a new partial-AUC surrogate.

claim: The experimental weighted persistent CVaR auxiliary loss after ten BCE epochs produced six valid evaluations. Precision and FAR worsened in all three pairs (mean -0.02182 and +0.0003667), runtime increased in every pair (+3.07667 seconds), and low-FAR recall had zero strict wins (mean -0.0070567). Mean ROS/F1/AUPRC changed -0.3544465/-0.00343/-0.0029933. Bootstrap F1 std improved in all three pairs, but neither configuration passed all-seed predictive or resource gates. This one weighted adaptation and schedule does not invalidate the source method, nor establish independent generalization.
hypothesis: Keep tail_risk_weight zero. Inspect the surrogate's state dynamics and actual tail-phase checkpoint selection before tuning its strength or attributing failure to the underlying partial-AUC formulation.

claim: All 27 inner models executed the tail phase, with 328 to 2050 tail batches per model. Selected checkpoints were from that phase in 13 models (6/3/4 by seed), while 14 retained pre-tail checkpoints. Mean surrogate losses ranged 1.66083 to 3.66163 and positive auxiliary thresholds ranged 0.688146 to 0.945286; no zero-threshold fraction was observed. These aggregates rule out a wholly skipped stage, but do not establish state convergence or explain performance causally. They are not new benchmark results.
hypothesis: Keep the tail branch disabled by default. Before changing its weight, measure whether weighted exceedance mass approaches beta on training data; finite auxiliary values alone are not evidence of a correctly estimated tail.

claim: For all 27 final inner models, positive-weighted mean negative exceedance mass was above beta=0.002: range 0.003683 to 0.011930, mean 0.006713. Mean weighted absolute per-positive beta gap was 0.006302. This measures final model/final auxiliary state, not selected checkpoints or external FPR. Exact stationary-interval fractions were zero, but finite-sample discreteness means that fact alone is not a convergence test. The measured mass discrepancy shows the current auxiliary updates do not accurately localize the requested empirical tail at training end.
hypothesis: Before increasing model-loss strength, test training-only empirical weighted-tail initialization or refresh of auxiliary thresholds, using exact tiny examples to check the quantile condition. Keep the same beta and benchmark gates; do not claim the diagnostic establishes a generalization benefit.

claim: With CVaR weight 0.01 fixed, epoch-wise training-only weighted-tail refresh improved recall_at_far in 3/3 seeds (mean +0.0119033) and score in 2/3 (+0.393855), but false alarm rate rose in all three (+0.000144667), precision fell on average (-0.00342667), AP fell (-0.00142667), and runtime rose (+1.30333 seconds). Neither arm passed all-seed predictive or resource gates. This is not an independent generalization test or a comparison against zero CVaR.
hypothesis: Directly compare refreshed CVaR against zero CVaR on matched seeds before retaining it; do not infer transitive improvements across seed sets.

claim: Direct comparison of refreshed CVaR weight 0.01 versus zero CVaR on seeds 20270426/27/28: F1 and F1_p10 improved in all three (+0.00289667/+0.00177333), but AP (-0.00528333), low-FAR recall (-0.00529333) and runtime (+2.33667 seconds) worsened in all three. Mean score -0.175593, precision -0.0350367, FAR +0.000377667. Both arms failed all-seed predictive and resource gates. This is training-seed stability on reused validation, not independent generalization.
hypothesis: Do not promote CVaR or tail refresh into the default search. Stop this fixed-weight route absent new evidence: improving the CVaR control was not a gain against the zero-CVaR reference. Prioritize a different mechanism addressing low-FAR ranking and runtime jointly.

claim: One train-only cProfile replay of candidate10 at seed20270429 measured 23.2839 seconds instrumented wall time. Nine fit_tree_branch calls accumulated 3.69802 seconds; 18 QuantileTransformer.transform calls accumulated 3.86756 seconds. Nested cumulative times overlap and include CPU synchronization waits; this is not isolated GPU timing or benchmark runtime. Features and full query inference are excluded, and the dummy query has two training rows.
hypothesis: Investigate optional fold-local reuse of preprocessing and tree predictions across neural replicas. Current replica seeds alter quantile subsampling and trees, so sharing changes predictions and requires matched benchmark validation; do not describe it as numerically equivalent or assume it solves the runtime gate.

claim: Sharing preprocessing within each fold versus independent replica preprocessing on seeds20270430/20270501/02 reduced runtime in 3/3 seeds (mean -5.98 seconds) and improved AP in 3/3 (+0.000353333). Mean score +0.101964 (2 wins), precision +0.00528667, recall -0.00661, F1 +0.000686667, low-FAR recall +0.00088 (1 win), FAR -0.0000663333, F1 bootstrap std +0.000206667. Both arms failed all-seed predictive and resource gates. This is reused-validation training-seed stability, not independent generalization.
hypothesis: Retain sharing as an optional runtime candidate, not a promoted default. A next isolated experiment can reuse tree predictions within a fold while keeping preprocessing shared in both arms; test whether reduced tree diversity harms low-FAR ranking. Do not infer that preprocessing alone solves all runtime or predictive gates.

claim: With shared preprocessing enabled in both arms, reusing fold-local tree predictions at seeds20270503/04/05 preserved every reported paired predictive metric and bootstrap standard deviation exactly, while reducing runtime in 3/3 seeds by mean 2.74333 seconds (21.3867 to18.6433 seconds). This is equality of evaluator-reported metrics, not proof of bitwise prediction equality or equivalence on all datasets/configurations. Neither arm passed all-seed predictive or resource gates against all ML baselines.
hypothesis: Retain shared preprocessing plus shared tree as a promising accelerated configuration for subsequent direct evaluation against the original reference. Do not add speed gains from different seed sets or claim generalization. Current runtime still exceeds the fast ML baselines; further work must address both low-FAR ranking and runtime.

claim: Direct paired comparison of shared fold preprocessing plus shared tree against original candidate10 at seeds20270506/07/08: runtime improved in3/3 (mean -8.69333 seconds,28.61 to19.9167) and low-FAR recall improved in3/3 (+0.00926). Mean score +0.198747 (2wins), AP +0.00044 (2wins), F1 +0.000293333 (2wins), recall +0.0119033, but precision -0.0115667 and FAR +0.000111333. Both arms failed all-seed predictive/resource gates. This is reused-validation training-seed stability, not independent generalization.
hypothesis: Use dual reuse as an optional efficient experimental branch, retaining the original reference. Further changes must improve precision/FAR without sacrificing the low-FAR ranking gain; do not promote it as universally superior or add gains across different seed sets.

claim: With both fold-sharing options enabled, fused AdamW reduced runtime in3/3 seeds20270509/10/11 (mean -1.18667 seconds), but AP worsened in3/3 (-0.00140667) and bootstrap F1 std worsened in3/3 (+0.000263333). Mean score -0.0466331 (1win), F1 -0.000596667, low-FAR recall -0.00088, recall -0.00352667, precision -0.000753333, FAR -0.0000223333. Both arms failed all-seed predictive/resource gates. Numerical optimizer equivalence is not established; reused validation does not establish independent generalization.
hypothesis: Keep the default optimizer unchanged. The modest time gain does not justify promoting a configuration with consistent AP and stability regressions. Preserve dual reuse as an optional branch and pursue predictive mechanisms or larger structural runtime reductions.

claim: On the dual-reuse branch with ordinary AdamW, reducing replicas3 to1 at seeds20270512/13/14 improved runtime in3/3 (19.0 to11.35 seconds, -7.65) and F1_p10 in3/3 (+0.00201). Mean score +0.0467529 but only1win; F1 +0.00200333, AP +0.000856667, recall +0.0110233. Low-FAR recall -0.00396667, precision -0.00342, FAR +0.000078. Both arms failed all-seed predictive/resource gates. Total time allowance stays240 seconds, so per-model allowance increases; epochs and learning rate are fixed. Reused-validation seed stability is not independent generalization.
hypothesis: Retain the single-replica configuration as an explicit efficiency option, not a default promotion. Its low-FAR ranking still needs improvement; avoid repeating a larger ensemble solely on intuition or treating runtime reductions as comprehensive superiority.

claim: On the dual-reuse single-replica branch, increasing lr0.0003 to0.001 at seeds20270515/16/17 changed mean score -0.333600 (1win), precision -0.01863, recall +0.01984, F1 -0.00719667, F1_p10 -0.00498667, AP -0.00339333, low-FAR recall +0.000883333 (1win), FAR +0.000289 and runtime -0.116667 seconds. Both arms failed all-seed predictive/resource gates. Earlier joint learning-rate/replica/epoch findings do not isolate this intervention. Reused-validation seed stability is not independent generalization.
hypothesis: Retain lr0.0003 for this branch. The negligible mean speed gain and unfavorable precision/F1/FAR tradeoff do not justify promotion; seek a mechanism improving ranking rather than further increasing the learning rate.

claim: On the dual-reuse single-replica branch, replacing TCN temporal mean with zero-initialized learned temporal weights at seeds20270518/19/20 produced no strict wins for score, F1, F1_p10, low-FAR recall, bootstrap std or runtime. Mean score -0.313993, F1 -0.00353333, F1_p10 -0.00344, AP -0.00209, low-FAR recall -0.00397, precision -0.00462, FAR +0.0000443333 and runtime +0.456667 seconds; mean recall was effectively unchanged. Both arms failed all-seed predictive/resource gates. This experiment does not refute every attention design or establish independent generalization.
hypothesis: Retain temporal mean pooling. Do not expand this lightweight attention route without new evidence; small parameter count and mean-equivalent initialization did not produce better ranking or efficiency.
